title_en: 99 Incredible Little Details in Grand Theft Auto 6 - Gameplay, Secrets, and Easter Eggs in GTA 6
summary_en: From gameplay quirks to secrets and Easter eggs, here are 99 incredible little details in Grand Theft Auto 6. Don’t worry, you’ll find no story spoilers here.
body_en:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here, and we’re finally getting to see what Rockstar has been cooking up for the last decade-and-change. It may be a studio already famous for its unbridled attention to detail, but just how many more tiny flourishes, references, and opportunities for emergent hilarity has Rockstar stuffed into GTA 6? The answer is a lot, so let’s get straight to it: here are 99 incredible little details in Grand Theft Auto 6. And don’t worry, you’ll find no story spoilers here.
1. From the get-go, it appears Rockstar has left no box unchecked. That is, during the Prologue, there’s a strong chance you’ll be successfully captured by the VCPD before you can effect a getaway. However, if you do manage to escape, you’ll get an extra segment of gameplay after the prison counselor addresses your initial evasion, in which she may even name-check the vehicle you used.
2. GTA 6’s selection of radio stations and podcasts is fabulous, and massively stocked with songs. Want to hear them when you’re outside of a car? You can purchase earbuds at an electronics store so that you can tune in via your phone.
3. Blood stains remain in the world for multiple days, so you may well receive a reminder of some poor behaviour on your part, even after sleeping and returning to the same spot in the days that follow.
4. Gang hideouts will reveal themselves all over the map as you progress, but one of the first you’ll probably find is an illegal animal smuggling operation tucked away in Jason’s hometown. Make sure you listen to the parrot for a clue to find more loot.
5. Speaking of animals, keep in mind that dogs will protect their owners, so consider that before you insult anyone out walking their best friend.
6. It’s also common to come across animals fighting amongst themselves, but if you spook them, they’ll typically scarper.
7. And no, it doesn’t appear that crocodiles take much interest in unconscious people that you may dump near them. But when they wake up, all bets are off.
8. The highly impressive blood tech will realistically coat surfaces the claret touches, such as covering a croc’s snout after snacking on an unfortunate fellow’s head.
9. Don’t park your car too close to the basketball hoop outside Jason’s first house. Even a well-placed shot could smash the windows of your ride.
10. Of course, cars can suffer considerably more than a busted windscreen, and car damage in GTA 6 is ludicrously good. Panels buckle dramatically, parts fall off, and dents appear exactly where they should.
11. Lose a wheel and the unfortunate rotor scraping against the asphalt will glow bright red as it dramatically heats up.
12. There’s a distinct difference in paint quality between hasty Pay ’n’ Spray jobs and professional recoats at a dedicated auto shop. Pay ’n’ Sprays offer extremely limited colours, and the paint finish has a noticeable “orange peel” effect.
13. Car glass isn’t perfect and, in the right light, you can see lots of scuffs, scratches, and imperfections.
14. Wipers will even leave visible streaks on the glass during rain, even though that’s something you’d only ever see rarely in the first-person view.
15. Businesses have their own vehicles, and you’ll spot vans and trucks across the map with all kinds of corporate and small business logos plastered on them. We’re still seeing ones we haven’t noticed, even after 120 hours, and it greatly increases the feeling of vehicle variety on the road.
16. The details on cars even extend to the fact that they have animated drivetrains – you can more easily spot when you flip a car, so take this as an excuse to get a little chaotic.
17. Some cars even have under-door lighting – an incredibly subtle effect you may well only occasionally see at night.
18. Brakes glow as a result of heavy use.
19. Superchargers make a very distinct noise, and your engine will sound different once you install them.
20. Vehicles have functioning indicators and windows, and you may even spot NPCs rolling up their windows if you’re annoying them. To use your own blinkers, tap left and right on the D-pad.
21. Truck nuts on vehicles. That’s it. No, they don’t shrink in the cold, but I’m not holding that against it.
22. Alongside the massive number of regular vehicles to discover, there are many unique vehicles sporting huge, custom decorations to find. One is a bright pink fan for a seafood restaurant that has “Our Shrimp so Pimp” painted on it.
23. There are also much, much cooler examples, including a very, very familiar Fast and Furious-adjacent green sports car with a custom paint job, tucked away in the largest house on Vespucci Island. The plate is the perfect touch, too: HAD YOU.
24. Like the cars, boats have also been lavished with attention to detail, and are typically christened with their own individual names, just like in real life.
25. And on that note, boats can now be physically launched from boat trailers, retrieved from the water again, and towed to anywhere else on the map. Same goes for jet skis and kayaks.
26. Cars and motorcycles can also be manually loaded onto trailers and towed anywhere you want. It doesn’t get around the tracker system, so it isn’t a method to cheat the new security features, but it’s still fun to fool around with.
27. Not only are jumbo jets way, way more authentically scaled – seriously, they’re huge now – but you need to enter them physically and walk to the cockpit to fly them.
28. Hijacking an enormous commercial airliner isn’t a thing the authorities will ignore or quickly forget. Soon after takeoff, you’ll be flanked by a pair of fighter jets who’ll order you to land, and shoot you down if you don’t. Jumbos are tougher than ever and will survive direct strikes from smaller aircraft, like choppers, but maybe it’s best to follow their orders.
29. Seriously, if you can see it, there’s a pretty good chance you can use it or drive it. This includes mundane work equipment like scissor lifts…
30. Excavators with huge claws…
31. Forklifts (which, unlike in GTA 5, are now strong enough to lift cars)...
32. And mobility scooters. They’re not quick (obviously), but if you’d thought, surely we can’t drive those ; think again.
33. We haven’t found a go-kart at this point, but here’s hoping something eventually unlocks at the as-yet unopened go-kart track, Hot Skidz, located next to the Frontier mini golf course near Belville.
34. The out-of-order arcade cabinets you’ll spot around the world all seem to have different notes and warning signs indicating they’re busted; it’s not just a single repeated texture.
35. Not all arcade cabinets are out-of-order, though; be sure to check out GTA 6’s cheeky take on Buck Hunter in Jason’s local bar.
36. Early in the game, the band performing at The Rusty Anchor plays unique covers of songs that don’t feature on GTA 6’s radio stations, including songs direct from the original GTA: Vice City. We won’t spoil which ones, but listen up when you encounter them.
37. The cane burning taking place at one of the map’s farms is a great visual, and just one of dozens and dozens of authentic little environmental surprises and flourishes going on around the map.
38. Have you found the Christmas house in Key Lento? Once you do, make sure you find the Christmas dog, who is dressed up in green and red and ready for pets.
39. The Vice City sign welcoming tourists to the city is right where it needs to be for planes to come right over it. Michael Bay, eat your heart out.
40. You can enter Vice City’s massive airport terminal in free-roam, but you definitely shouldn’t move through airport security armed with the kind of hardware Jason and Lucia are always carrying. It probably won’t work out great for you.
41. The attention to detail extends all the way down to blink-and-you’ll-miss-them props. For instance, did GTA 6 need to have multiple power drill brands? Probably not, but it does – including a Dewalt knock-off Device, complete with yellow and black detailing.
42. Many props feature the tiniest of text you can only read if you focus on it. A can of lubricant does feel like a slight missed opportunity for more jokes, but, hey, it does at least improve penetration.
43. Rest assured there are subtle jokes galore all over the map for those willing to explore – certainly more than we can list here. These range from massive billboards with ridiculous images on, to small stealth gags on sticky note-sized pieces of paper.
44. Be sure to check your phone for all sorts of useful information. The weather app will give you the forecast for the next day, for example.
45. Surfing social media can ping new contacts and pin activities to your map well before you’d drive past them naturally.
46. Likewise, checking out physical notice boards can do exactly the same thing.
47. Skimming through magazines can also ping new discoveries.
48. There are animations for all manner of circumstances, depending on a whole bunch of factors. For instance, if you start to jog while carrying a six-pack of beer, the characters will quickly tuck it up under their armpit and carry it like a football to protect it.
49. If both your character’s hands are full, there’s a different animation for opening a chip packet with your teeth, as opposed to using two hands.
50. Similarly, there’s a distinct animation for opening cans of drink with one hand if necessary.
51. There are also different animations for opening doors when your hands are full, as the characters will use their shoulders rather than grabbing the doorknob.
52. On the topic of doors, if you park up against an object or your spot is too cramped, there’s also a different animation where your character will only open car doors partially, and subsequently shuffle out of the gap sideways.
53. And on the topic of knobs, there are.. a lot of male members in full flight in GTA 6, but, to be fair, nudity is very much a two-way street here with people of all shapes, sizes, and genders letting it all hang out.
54. You can open car doors for your partner, and it makes them fall extra in love with you, boosting your relationship stat.
55. Jason and Lucia each have a side of the bed they’ll always lie on, wherever they’re staying.
56. Getting physically close to your partner as you fall deeper in love can trigger a silent heartbeat effect in your controller.
57. We haven’t even talked about the hair yet, which is basically witchcraft. The way it moves and slides across their shoulders, or whips in the wind, or floats and sways in the water. It’s ridiculously good.
58. This isn’t the only insanely pretty technical achievement GTA 6 makes, however, and it’s honestly tough to choose what graphical astonishment is the most remarkable. Water is an absolutely massive highlight, which was an utter necessity for the geography of Vice City and its surroundings. This goes all the way from the immediately showstopping quantity of the swell and waves…
59. …to the smaller stuff you’ll notice as you really begin to pay attention. Maybe that’s the concentric rings being whipped up by helicopter downwash.
60. Or maybe it’s the countless overlapping ripples caused in the water by rain.
61. Maybe it’s the expanding splashwave you get after tossing a bloke into the water.
62. Or maybe it’s the subtle wake he generates sheepishly swimming back to shore.
63. Maybe it’s the fact that the splash seems to get bigger the higher you toss people in from.
64. Maybe it’s the uncanny quality of the refraction.
65. Or maybe it’s the fact that fish cast shadows properly underwater, even while the surface is still reflecting everything above and refracting everything below!
66. Maybe it’s a different fluid entirely, like the way drinks disappear gradually as characters sip them.
67. Heck, the attention to detail extends further than just what liquids look like – it’s sound, too. Yes, there are completely different sound effects for putting down a full can of drink compared to an empty one.
68. Or is it the ludicrously pretty lighting – particularly how insanely good dawn and dusk look?
69. It’s a tough question because, seriously, it only really gets better when the sun goes down. Check out the wildly realistic shadows, all occurring authentically in real-time in the midst of everything else GTA 6 is doing.
70. Check out the glow of light in water. It looks ridiculously good.
71. We haven’t even mentioned the effectiveness of reflecting light off surfaces like the bright sheen on road signs from harsh headlights, or the highly realistic strips of cat’s eyes lining the roads.
72. And, look, if we want to talk about reflections, the TV is mirrored in the glass frames behind the couch.
73. The shiny chrome work on a truck will also reflect surrounding details. It simply doesn’t stop; everywhere you look, something eye-catching is happening, or there’s something to hear.
74. RydeMe drivers hate it when you don’t close the door for them.
75. And if you ever cross a driver, you’ll be temporarily banned from using the app for fast travel.
76. Hop into a chopper after sprinting and you’ll hear your character still catching their breath as they put on their headset.
77. The World War 2 novel in Jason’s first house leans heavily into the classic hometown nickname trope for its soldiers, only they’re all in-universe GTA cities, like Liberty, Gellhorn, Alderney, and Carcer.
78. Thrown knives will get embedded in walls and doors, and can even open doors from the force of the impact.
79. You can manually raise and lower bridges over the various waterways and create insane jumps.
80. Pool balls collect dots of chalk dust on them.
81. Clothes only get wet up to the point you were in the water.
82. Punching bags are crushed temporarily where you strike them.
83. You can leap out of moving buses when commuting on them.
84. There are multiple references to the prolific “before GTA 6” meme, including a social post decrying the fact that the Barnyard Blue video game arrived before Race ’n’ Chase 7, and a Righteous Slaughter T-shirt making a similar gag. Righteous Slaughter on the JoySystem when?
85. Speaking of the JoySystem, the indie walking simulator Tenebrae Lux is credited to a fictional creator called Johannes Zuch, who’s Bogarted the whole production and whose name appears relentlessly on screen throughout. In other words, it walks like a walking simulator, but it quacks like a Hideo Kojima parody.
86. Speaking of Bogart, I don’t know how many GTA 6 players are going to be familiar with the 1948 Humphrey Bogart noir film Key Largo, but I appreciate GTA’s take: The Key Lento, which can be found in a collection of thrift shop DVDs on the island.
87. Unlike GTA 5, GTA 6 has a host of different fast food chains you can enter. You can even use the drive-thrus.
88. The physics handling the dragging objects behind your cars is genuinely brilliant. In fact, there’s so much Fast & Furious in this game I’m very surprised I haven’t stumbled across an ejecto seato yet, cuz. That was the one set in Miami, after all.
89. Some clocks are animated and show the right in-game time at any given moment.
90. Characters will automatically rest sunglasses on top of their heads when they get home, and drop them back over their eyes when they leave.
91. You can find a mini Arthur Morgan riding an equally tiny dog at Frontier Mini Golf.
92. You can also find Arthur’s cowboy hat at a Port Gellhorn yard sale.
93. If that’s not your style, you can always opt for a McClane Ventilation Specialists hat from the Hamlet thrift store. Die-hard fans of McClane’s ventilation expertise will even be able to find his actual warehouse a few streets across town.
94. In a room near the top of a tower, near Donnie’s trailer, is an old analogue TV that displays the logo for GTA: Vice City’s Malibu Club. Or, at least, it does once you flip a switch and hit a button.
95. The pre-order bonus ’55 Vapid Stanier car is available from the Ocean View Hotel from Chapter 3 onward. In GTA Vice City, you’d often see similar Oceanics sitting in front of that game’s version of the Ocean View.
96. In The Rusty Anchor bar, you’ll find a vintage poster of Love Fist’s 1986 Dogs on Heat Tour, the year of GTA: Vice City, though Love Fist also overtly exists in GTA’s current HD universe. There’s a Fatal Incursion poster below, another in-universe band from GTA 5, albeit one we actually don’t know much about.
97. GTA: Vice City’s Phil Cassidy is reborn in GTA 6 as the proprietor of Phil’s Ammu-Nation, and star of the greatest commercial on GTA 6’s TV channels. No ifs, no buts.
98. Speaking of butts, however, good luck convincing anyone we need new consoles when we’re getting fully-modelled goose pimples on butt skin these days. We’re in the endgame now, ladies and gentlemen.
99. And finally, yes, if you climb to the top of the tall tower you can find just outside of Hamlet, you will find an easter egg up there. That’s the end of the sentence.
What discoveries have you made so far? What are the tiny details impressing you? Let us know in the comments. We’ll no doubt be back for another 99 in the future.
